references.text: Both verses illustrate the recurring life rhythm in the genealogies before the Flood, where each generation has a son and then lives long to have more children.
The verses show continuity in the lineage but also mark the theological transition from pre- to post-Flood through the marked reduction in lifespan.
The verses are direct parallels within the same chapter showing that Mahalalel shares the same life rhythm and God's blessing as Adam, and is thus part of the original creation order.
The verses are direct parallels within the same chapter showing the direct father-son connection and the recurring life rhythm in the same generation.
The verses are direct parallels within the same chapter showing that Mahalalel is part of the same line that begins with Seth, and that all these fathers share the same life rhythm.
